title: Space bound for the amplified machine
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape alphabet, let $r$ be a natural number, and let $d:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean-valued function. Suppose $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ bounds the space used by $N$ on every Boolean input word $x$ and every choice word $w$, when started on $x$. Then, for every such $x$ and $w$, the space used by the amplified machine on input $x$ under choices $w$ is at most $(r+1)k(2s(|x|)+1)$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $N$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbol alphabet
$d$ is a function from natural numbers to Boolean values
For every Boolean input word $x$ and choice word $w$, the space used by $N$ from its initial configuration on $x$ is at most $s(|x|)$
